## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One problem needs fixing: when a setting is adopted through the command, its "Adopted" message now prints twice. `plan` already emits adoption progress, and `run` now prints the new `adopt` entry as well. The audit entry is excluded from command output as intended, and the new test covers that.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/planner.py:9 — correctness — Calling `run({"theme": "dark"}, {"theme": "dark"}, messages.append)` now produces `["Adopted theme", "Adopted theme"]` instead of one adoption line. `plan` still calls `emit(f"Adopted {name}")` on line 8 and now also appends `{"kind": "adopt", ...}`. `app/cli.py:6-9` emits the message of every change that is not an audit entry, so the adoption is reported once during planning and again when changes are rendered. To fix it, keep the progress emit in `plan` and have `run` skip `"adopt"` entries alongside `"audit"` (or skip any kind that `plan` already emitted). Then add a `run` test with an existing setting that asserts `messages == ["Adopted theme"]`. No current test calls `run` with a setting that is already present: `test_adoption_progress` calls `plan` directly. — Every adopted setting now shows up twice in command output, which contradicts the PR description's "retaining progress output during adoption". No test catches this regression.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `app/cli.py:7-8` already filters out `"audit"` entries, and `tests/test_planner.py:17-21` checks both that the audit record is returned and that it is not printed.
